commentary.label: Tier list Part 1 (2023)
commentary.summary: The Legend of Bumbo is a Candy Crush-style match-puzzle roguelike built on The Binding of Isaac, with an all-cardboard look. He loves the art style and the core gameplay concept. He thinks the game feels rushed and unfinished, with run-losing bugs, very long fights and heavy RNG. There is little left to do once every character has been played. He places it in mid B tier and says he wishes he could rate it higher.
praise: Unique cardboard art style across the trailer and the actual gameplay
Fun core gameplay and design concept of a match-puzzle roguelike
Reuses Binding of Isaac enemies in a fresh format
Strategy depth, with the ability to find very broken combos
High potential if it had been polished
criticism: Game-breaking bugs cost him runs several times and forced restarts
Encounters can drag on; one turn took about 30 minutes
Heavy RNG, and the first turn of a fight can doom a run
Little left to do after playing every character
unique_points: Candy Crush-like match gameplay combined with a Binding of Isaac roguelike
Everything in the game is made of cardboard, not just the trailer
Combos can get broken but RNG can also ruin a run
commentary.quote: I just wish there was more love put into this game
design_criteria: Art style/charm: cardboard look is unique and praised
Core gameplay design: loved, though execution is flawed
Run/encounter length: fights can last an eternity
RNG vs strategy: luck can decide a run, broken combos possible
Replayability/content: little to do after all characters played

community.one_liner: A match-3 puzzle deckbuilding roguelite, cardboard-craft prequel to The Binding of Isaac, by Edmund McMillen, James Interactive and Ridiculon.
community.consensus_summary: Players rate it Very Positive on Steam (about 81% of roughly 5.9k reviews in our data), while Metacritic sits at a Mixed 73 critic / 6.4 user. The core loop of matching tiles to cast spells and building a loadout is widely called addictive and charming, but it is held back by heavy RNG, thin explanation, a grindy unlock system and lots of bugs. Development was rocky: the original programmer left, and the last official patches came around 2021 before a later community-linked 'Windfall' update was announced. Many negative Steam reviews read like 'fun game, but unfinished and buggy', so the score is dragged down by polish rather than by the core idea.
best_things: The match-tiles-to-cast-spells loop is satisfying and addictive, with big combo turns feeling great when a board lines up
Cardboard cut-out art style and child-like Isaac-prequel atmosphere are charming
Deckbuilder-style decisions (skills, items, trinkets) pay off when you plan around the board
100+ items, 80+ trinkets, several playable characters and 10 bosses give a decent item pool
Isaac-style humor and lore expansion appeal strongly to Binding of Isaac fans
Ridiculon soundtrack is praised (Steam tags include Great Soundtrack)
worst_things: Very buggy: softlocks (especially from clicking too fast), run resets, broken puzzle boards and visual glitches
Achievements and unlocks often fail to trigger or duplicate; players resort to third-party fixes
Steam achievements are so unreliable that players say a third-party fix (the Windfall mod) is practically required; the last official patch was around March 2021
Save data can be lost, and saves are local rather than properly cloud-synced
Heavy luck dependence: a bad board or a room with 5-6 enemies can end a run before you act
Little is explained, so boss and enemy mechanics become knowledge checks
Limited content at launch (four dungeons) and the game feels unfinished or abandoned to many
Critics called the UI feedback (tooltips, tile highlighting) unpolished and mobile-like
improvements: Fix the long list of bugs, achievement issues and save problems
Reduce run-ending RNG from board draws and enemy stacking, and tighten balance
Explain enemy and boss mechanics in-game instead of relying on trial and error
Rework the slot-machine-style item unlock system so progress is not so grindy
Add more content and more creative synergy/deckbuilding options, since many builds feel samey
Improve UI feedback such as tooltips and tile highlighting
unique_things: Mixes a match-3 board game with roguelite deckbuilding and Isaac-style items
Handmade cardboard look and tone, as a literal toy-theatre prequel to Isaac
Spells are fueled by matching colored tile types, so board reading and spell planning interlock
Gross-out Isaac humor applied to puzzle combat (for example flinging excrement at enemies)
Edmund McMillen's biggest project by his own account, after a roughly four-year development
tedious_or_disliked: Unlocking new items is gated behind a chance-based system that only rolls after winning long runs, so the grind is painful
Some later areas and progress are gated behind playing specific characters
Limited coins per floor make stat upgrades and shops feel too scarce
Enemies that resist everything or multi-hit counters can make turns feel unfair
Repetitive play over extended sessions, per critics
divisive_points: Price: some call $15 too steep for the content and state; others find it worth it
Difficulty and RNG: some see it as tense roguelite variance, others as unfair and unwinnable runs
Whether it is a real roguelike with synergies or an easy game that lacks roguelike depth without them
community.reception_notes: Launched on Steam in Nov 2019 with softlock issues; programmer James Interactive could not continue, so McMillen brought in Isaac: Rebirth programmers in late 2020. Ports followed: Android (Dec 2020), Epic/GOG (Feb 2022), Switch/PS5/Xbox (June 2022). Steam reviews note the last official update was around March 2021 and that a third-party mod called Windfall is treated as near-required for achievements and fixes. A Steam community thread titled Windfall Update 1.5 was posted in May (year unclear, I could not read its contents), so it is unclear whether this is now official. OpenCritic score could not be verified: web search budget was exhausted and the guessed OpenCritic URL returned a different game, so the value is null. Steam revenue estimates from local data: ~$2.97M gross, ~$876k net, owners 1-2M (estimate from Boxleiter-style sources, order of magnitude only). Reddit could not be fetched, so community detail relies on Steam reviews and discussion pages.
